messages:
nina-eng: Hey team, quick heads-up: planning to relocate briefly to Lisbon for 3 months (June 1 -> Aug 31). It's a remote writing/research stint, no local contractors or client meetings. Do I need to update my homebase? How will the WFH stipend work? Any payroll/tax steps?

sam-peopleops: Thanks Nina. For a 3-month stay (90 days) we treat it as a short-term remote. Please keep your legal homebase as-is unless you plan to move indefinitely. WFH stipend: monthly and prorated if you change homebase mid-month; otherwise it continues. Submit the "temporary remote" form and tag me.

tasha-payroll: Nina - confirm your legal homebase and the Lisbon address. If you stay more than 30 days in any rolling 12-month window in Portugal, we need to monitor for tax/residency flags. Payroll will track days and advise if we need to withhold locally. Also note payroll cutoffs: any required tax changes take effect next payroll cycle after forms processed.

leo-legal: Adding that while an individual 3-month remote stint rarely triggers corporate nexus, Portugal and many EU jurisdictions have employee tax/residence rules that can create personal obligations (income tax, social contributions) if you establish tax residency. Recommend you maintain ties to your legal homebase and avoid formal housing contracts that look like permanent residency. If you plan to accept local bank transfers or contract local services, let us know.

benefits-bot: Benefits reminder: check your medical network. EU stays may make your US-based plan out-of-network. Telemedicine options might be limited; save receipts for reimbursements.

nina-eng: Plan is to keep CA as homebase, maintain US bank account, and use short-term Airbnb bookings. No local employment or contracting. Will submit the form now.

sam-peopleops: Perfect. Once we receive the form we

will flag payroll to watch the 30-day rule and add a note to your benefits file. Safe travels! :airplane:
